question:
RULE on PR #239. Review verdict is NO-GO: four Material findings, one Needs decision, nine Deferred risk, nine Polish. Three of the four Material findings are ordinary correction work and route back to implementation without your involvement. The fourth is yours alone, because its remedy changes contract text this PR promotes into SECURITY.md.

R1: the probe writes inside the user's repository and executes a program the repository selects, on the happy path, in any git-lfs repository. A committed .gitattributes travels with a clone and needs no local config; when an entry goes racy — same size, touched mtime, which is the normal state of a repository a live session was just editing — git must run the clean filter to compare, git spawns git-lfs filter-process, and git-lfs installs an executable .git/hooks/pre-push. The FO reproduced this independently with a matched control. Both flags worked exactly as designed and .git/index never moved; the write went through a path neither bound contemplated. This falsifies, in text THIS PR ADDS to SECURITY.md, Invariant 2's "neither writes there nor executes anything the repository supplies" — both halves — plus the section's violation list and AC2.

No argv-only fix exists: filter driver names are unbounded so no -c filter.X.clean= generalises, and an in-tree .gitattributes beats core.attributesFile. So the remedy is contract wording, a third bound if one exists, or a narrower feature. Deciding which is your call under the workflow's own rule that only the captain changes approved scope or accepted value. Rejecting routes R1 through R4 back to implementation as correction round 1.

artifacts.summary:
Full adversarial as scoped: four lenses and a completeness critic run as separated passes, arbitrated by reproduction. Nothing was edited and no commit was made on the PR branch.

What is clean, and measured rather than read. AC3, the off-thread dispatch, is the best-built part of this PR and is over-determined rather than under: the lock oracle does not stub the spawn, so the prober genuinely runs on the probe thread; the acceptance criterion's own named falsifier was run thirty times in a throwaway copy and failed thirty out of thirty, with four sibling tests deadlocking outright; submit returns in 0.115 ms with the probe blocked, and thirty real SessionEnd posts through the full hook path delivered thirty out of thirty at a maximum of 11.71 ms against the two-second budget, a 170-fold margin. AC8, the promotion, is immaculate and was verified twice independently: the promoted span and the merged contract span are both 3232 bytes and 55 lines with identical sha256, diff silent, both amendments byte-identical, the plan document deleted in the same commit, and the validator exit zero. The null-at-the-wire surface was confirmed from real collect bytes rather than from the dataclass, and the eight-versus-two split was verified against the identity normalizers and the adapter maps, with the cycle-1 unsoundness confirmed not to have recurred. Both flags were re-measured as independently load-bearing at git 2.55.0.

The blocker, R1, was found at arbitration rather than by a lens: two lenses independently found the execute half and neither found the write. The remedy is captain-owned because it amends promoted contract text.

Three further Material findings route back without needing a ruling. R2: the staleness guard is vacuous whenever the finished stamp is zero, so a clean reading is republished as a false rather than a null over a session that kept working — the exact shape AC6 exists to prevent — and once the working overlay lapses at ninety seconds no branch nulls the pair, making it permanent. R3: the guard that would have caught R2 does not exist; two agents independently deleted all three reducer clears and forced the aggregate forward to none in throwaway copies and the suite stayed green at 253 and 213 tests, so the aggregate half of the feature could be dead on arrival with CI green. R4: the probe tests error rather than skip when git is absent, violating AC2's explicit clause, reproduced with a shim path as two errors and five skips where eleven skips were expected.

R6 is the sharpest gap: stripping both flags at the call site leaves the argv test green, because it pins the constant and nothing asserts what the probe function actually hands the runner. So the two behavioural hazard tests are the sole guard against a call-site regression — and those are exactly the ones the builder disclosed as vacuous on Windows, which the review confirmed and widened, since the script is written with CRLF line endings and the executable bit is a no-op there.

Two reproductions initially refuted their own findings and were only confirmed after the harness was built correctly — R2 by the reviewer, and R1 by the FO. Both are recorded as refuted-then-confirmed so that a first negative result is not mistaken for absence.
